text: A no-edit byte-identical round-trip test can pass while the serializer is untested: rhwp's HWP5 round-trip gate checked a raw-stream byte-replay path, and after re-running the edit-then-save path on a 429-document corpus it recorded 786 divergence rows, 103 of them defects (July 2026; the passthrough was later restricted to unchanged sections). Its later load/save sweep driving real 한글 2022 through COM on a 10k corpus found 163 documents losing body text after save round trips. A round trip alone does not prove the output is correct; the target application has to open it.
scope: One project's measurement (rhwp issue #2740, July 2026) plus one spreadsheet-project statement; generalisation to my app is my inference
next_action: Make the no-edit byte check only a smoke test; gate on an edit-path field sweep plus opening the saved files in real 한글

text: Proposal: do not write a new HWP engine. Build a native AppKit macOS shell on rhwp's Rust core (pinned tag, read-only upstream like HOP), and put the depth into a verification harness: a provenance-tracked corpus, edit-path field sweeps, and automated reopening in two real Hancom versions. First target L1 (text edits) saved as HWP and HWPX, with L2 next.

reviews.rationale: rhwp already claims HWP/HWPX save, so the engine need not be rewritten
HOP does not offer HWPX save in UI: a concrete gap a new shell could fill
Save fidelity is where existing apps fail in practice, so verification is where depth pays
Real 한글 is the decisive check for saved files (rejected file found only by opening in 한컴 2024)
Motivates using two Hancom versions as the reference
